reflectionText: Completing 18 university credits in Korean alongside my IT degree required strong discipline and consistency to master a new alphabet and grammatical structure. This perseverance enabled me to reach a solid A2/B1 level, laying the groundwork for my academic exchange in South Korea.

Practicing bouldering and climbing regularly taught me to approach each route like a technical puzzle: analyzing sequences, testing solutions, falling, and iterating until succeeding. This sport strengthens my stress management, physical balance, and resilience when facing complex challenges.

This demanding student job taught me how to stay calm and efficient during peak hours while adhering to strict operational standards. It helped me build strong reliability, teamwork, and priority management under pressure.

My exchange semester at Pusan National University has been a major milestone both academically—specializing in AI and Data Science—and personally. Living and studying in South Korea taught me to step out of my comfort zone and adapt smoothly to a multicultural environment.
These 132 hours of summer work helped me gain independence and quickly adapt to professional workplace expectations. I learned to stay organized and maintain consistent commitment over time.

This 100-hour team project introduced me to the realities of collaborative Full-Stack development, from React/Node.js architecture to resolving Git merge conflicts. I realized how vital clear team communication is to deliver a cohesive and reliable web platform.

This first hospitality role taught me customer service skills, active listening, and responsiveness on the floor. Coordinating orders with the kitchen gave me a solid foundation in communication and multitasking.

Troubleshooting hardware and software issues for family and friends taught me how to explain technical concepts in plain language. This hands-on practice sharpened my methodical diagnostic skills and patience with non-technical users.

Building an interactive game in Python allowed me to structure algorithmic logic, manage application states, and refine user experience. The main challenge was organizing clean modular code as a team to prevent interaction bugs.

reflectionText: Collaborating in English with international students on robotics and automation challenges broadened my perspective on teamwork. I learned to adapt quickly to different problem-solving approaches under tight deadlines.

Designing the PostgreSQL database for the climbing platform showed me that a clean relational schema is the backbone of any performant app. I learned to anticipate scalability needs and enforce data integrity right from the modeling phase.

reflectionText: Supporting fellow students in their IT coursework pushed me to structure and rephrase my knowledge so it stays clear and accessible. Teaching technical concepts proved to be the most effective way to deepen my own mastery.

Designing and routing a printed circuit board from scratch gave me a concrete understanding of the hardware layer beneath software. This project required precision to respect physical routing constraints and avoid connection flaws.

Building this portfolio from the ground up allowed me to combine modern front-end architecture, UI/UX design, and trilingual internationalization. I learned to structure a scalable, maintainable application tailored to showcase my technical identity.

Attending an IT exhibition in South Korea gave me firsthand insight into cutting-edge AI innovations and allowed me to connect with professionals in the Asian tech ecosystem. This experience fueled my curiosity and sharpened my awareness of current industry trends.
